diagnostics.title: Data fetching inside an effect

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Loading flag reset outside finally
diagnostics.message: This resets a loading/busy flag only on the success path: if the awaited call rejects the reset never runs and the flag stays stuck truthy (a spinner that never stops, a button disabled forever). Move the reset into a `finally` block, or mirror it on every catch, so it clears on rejection too.
diagnostics.help: A trailing `setLoading(false)` after an `await` never runs if the awaited call rejects, so the flag stays stuck truthy; reset it in a `finally` block (or mirror the reset on every catch) so it clears on both paths.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.title: createObjectURL without revokeObjectURL
diagnostics.message: `URL.createObjectURL(...)` pins the underlying Blob/File in memory, and this produced URL is not provably revoked. Store the URL and pass that same value to `URL.revokeObjectURL` once you're done so the Blob can be freed.
diagnostics.help: Call `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` once the object URL is no longer needed (after the download, in a `useEffect` cleanup, or on unmount). An object URL keeps its Blob/File alive for the document lifetime until it is revoked.

diagnostics.help: Keep state updater callbacks pure and return only the next state. Move notifications, storage, timers, ref writes, and other external work into the event or effect that queues the update.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Client fetch for server data
diagnostics.message: useEffect + fetch in a page/layout makes your users wait through an extra round trip & loading spinner.
diagnostics.help: Remove 'use client' and fetch directly in the Server Component. No API round-trip, and secrets stay on the server.

diagnostics.title: Data fetching inside an effect
diagnostics.message: fetch() inside useEffect can race, double-fire, or leak. Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component instead.
diagnostics.help: Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.help: Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

diagnostics.title: Missing effect dependencies
diagnostics.message: `useEffect` can run with a stale `DEFAULT_CARIBBEAN_ITINERARY` & show your users old data.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Array index result dereferenced without a guard

diagnostics.help: An array index read is typed `T` but is `T | undefined` at runtime, so dereferencing it on an empty list, a non-matching regex, or a short split throws. Add a length/emptiness check or optional chaining before the access.

diagnostics.help: Use a plain string path: `import('./feature/heavy.js')` so the bundler can split this into its own chunk.

diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Missing effect dependencies
diagnostics.message: `useEffect` can run with a stale `supabase.from` & show your users old data.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Effect subscription or timer never cleaned up
diagnostics.message: `subscribe` creates a subscription in useEffect without guaranteed cleanup. Return a cleanup function that owns every allocation so it does not leak after unmount.
diagnostics.help: Return a cleanup function that stops the subscription or timer: `return () => target.removeEventListener(name, handler)` for listeners, `return () => clearInterval(id)` or `clearTimeout(id)` for timers, `return () => observer.disconnect()` for observers, `return () => socket.close()` for connections, or `return unsubscribe` if the subscribe call already gave you one.

diagnostics.title: State adjusted after a prop changes
diagnostics.message: This effect adjusts state after a prop changes, so users briefly see the stale value.
diagnostics.help: Remove the adjustment effect by deriving values during render, resetting the component with a key, or updating related state in the event that changes the prop. Avoid tracking the previous prop in more state, which preserves the duplication. See https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#adjusting-some-state-when-a-prop-changes

diagnostics.title: Ref initializer runs on every render
diagnostics.message: useRef(now()) rebuilds this value on every render & throws it away.
diagnostics.help: Initialize the ref lazily so expensive values are not rebuilt and discarded on every render.

diagnostics.title: State updater has side effects
diagnostics.message: This state updater performs setTimeout(). React may run updater functions more than once, so side effects here can repeat or observe inconsistent external state.
diagnostics.help: Keep state updater callbacks pure and return only the next state. Move notifications, storage, timers, ref writes, and other external work into the event or effect that queues the update.

diagnostics.title: Side effect inside a state updater function
diagnostics.message: This side-effecting call runs inside a state updater, which React may invoke more than once. Move it outside the setter after computing the next state.
diagnostics.help: React may replay a state updater, so callbacks, analytics, and persistence inside it can run more than once. Compute state purely, then perform the side effect outside the setter.

diagnostics.title: Data fetching inside an effect
diagnostics.message: fetch() inside useEffect can race, double-fire, or leak. Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component instead.
diagnostics.help: Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

diagnostics.title: createObjectURL without revokeObjectURL
diagnostics.message: `URL.createObjectURL(...)` pins the underlying Blob/File in memory, and this produced URL is not provably revoked. Store the URL and pass that same value to `URL.revokeObjectURL` once you're done so the Blob can be freed.
diagnostics.help: Call `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` once the object URL is no longer needed (after the download, in a `useEffect` cleanup, or on unmount). An object URL keeps its Blob/File alive for the document lifetime until it is revoked.

diagnostics.title: await inside a loop

diagnostics.help: Collect the items, then use `await Promise.all(items.map(...))` so independent work runs at the same time

diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.title: Boolean toggle reads a stale value

diagnostics.help: Toggle boolean state with the functional updater `setX(previous => !previous)` so deferred callbacks always read the latest committed value.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check

diagnostics.title: Loading flag reset outside finally
diagnostics.message: This resets a loading/busy flag only on the success path: if the awaited call rejects the reset never runs and the flag stays stuck truthy (a spinner that never stops, a button disabled forever). Move the reset into a `finally` block, or mirror it on every catch, so it clears on rejection too.
diagnostics.help: A trailing `setLoading(false)` after an `await` never runs if the awaited call rejects, so the flag stays stuck truthy; reset it in a `finally` block (or mirror the reset on every catch) so it clears on both paths.

diagnostics.title: Effect promise .then sets state with no catch

diagnostics.title: Effect subscription or timer never cleaned up
diagnostics.message: `on` creates a subscription in useEffect without guaranteed cleanup. Return a cleanup function that owns every allocation so it does not leak after unmount.
diagnostics.help: Return a cleanup function that stops the subscription or timer: `return () => target.removeEventListener(name, handler)` for listeners, `return () => clearInterval(id)` or `clearTimeout(id)` for timers, `return () => observer.disconnect()` for observers, `return () => socket.close()` for connections, or `return unsubscribe` if the subscribe call already gave you one.

diagnostics.title: Ref mutated during render
diagnostics.message: This ref is mutated during render. React can replay or discard render work, so the mutation can leak from UI that never commits.
diagnostics.help: Move ref writes into an event handler or effect. Render must stay pure because React can replay or discard it. The predictable null-guarded lazy initialization pattern remains supported.

diagnostics.title: Loading flag reset outside finally
diagnostics.message: This resets a loading/busy flag only on the success path: if the awaited call rejects the reset never runs and the flag stays stuck truthy (a spinner that never stops, a button disabled forever). Move the reset into a `finally` block, or mirror it on every catch, so it clears on rejection too.
diagnostics.help: A trailing `setLoading(false)` after an `await` never runs if the awaited call rejects, so the flag stays stuck truthy; reset it in a `finally` block (or mirror the reset on every catch) so it clears on both paths.

diagnostics.title: Unversioned localStorage key
diagnostics.message: localStorage.setItem("7h_accounts", JSON.stringify(...)) has no version, so changing the data shape later crashes your users' saved sessions. Add one to the key (e.g. "7h_accounts:v1").
diagnostics.help: Put a version in the storage key (e.g. "myKey:v1"). If you change the data shape later, old saved data can be ignored instead of crashing the app.

diagnostics.message: fetch() inside useEffect can race, double-fire, or leak. Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component instead.

diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.message: This state updater performs queueMicrotask(). React may run updater functions more than once, so side effects here can repeat or observe inconsistent external state.
diagnostics.help: Keep state updater callbacks pure and return only the next state. Move notifications, storage, timers, ref writes, and other external work into the event or effect that queues the update.

diagnostics.title: Side effect inside a state updater function
diagnostics.message: This side-effecting call runs inside a state updater, which React may invoke more than once. Move it outside the setter after computing the next state.
diagnostics.help: React may replay a state updater, so callbacks, analytics, and persistence inside it can run more than once. Compute state purely, then perform the side effect outside the setter.

diagnostics.title: Unversioned localStorage key
diagnostics.message: localStorage.setItem("7h_crew_schedules", JSON.stringify(...)) has no version, so changing the data shape later crashes your users' saved sessions. Add one to the key (e.g. "7h_crew_schedules:v1").
diagnostics.help: Put a version in the storage key (e.g. "myKey:v1"). If you change the data shape later, old saved data can be ignored instead of crashing the app.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.title: Loading flag reset outside finally
diagnostics.message: This resets a loading/busy flag only on the success path: if the awaited call rejects the reset never runs and the flag stays stuck truthy (a spinner that never stops, a button disabled forever). diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Client fetch for server data
diagnostics.message: useEffect + fetch in a page/layout makes your users wait through an extra round trip & loading spinner.
diagnostics.help: Remove 'use client' and fetch directly in the Server Component. No API round-trip, and secrets stay on the server.

diagnostics.title: Data fetching inside an effect
diagnostics.message: fetch() inside useEffect can race, double-fire, or leak. Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component instead.
diagnostics.help: Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Client fetch for server data
diagnostics.message: useEffect + fetch in a page/layout makes your users wait through an extra round trip & loading spinner.
diagnostics.help: Remove 'use client' and fetch directly in the Server Component. No API round-trip, and secrets stay on the server.

diagnostics.title: Data fetching inside an effect
diagnostics.message: fetch() inside useEffect can race, double-fire, or leak. Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component instead.
diagnostics.help: Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Effect promise .then sets state with no catch
diagnostics.message: This promise chain runs in an effect, ends in a `.then` that sets state or mutates a ref, and has no `.catch` or enclosing try/catch, so a rejection leaves the state unset and surfaces as an unhandled rejection. Add a `.catch` handler on the chain (`.finally` does not count).
diagnostics.help: An async init in an effect that sets state in `.then` but has no `.catch` leaves the component stuck and raises an unhandled rejection when it fails. Add a `.catch` on the chain (`.finally` does not handle the rejection).

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.help: Keep state updater callbacks pure and return only the next state. Move notifications, storage, timers, ref writes, and other external work into the event or effect that queues the update.

diagnostics.title: Side effect inside a state updater function
diagnostics.message: This side-effecting call runs inside a state updater, which React may invoke more than once. Move it outside the setter after computing the next state.
diagnostics.help: React may replay a state updater, so callbacks, analytics, and persistence inside it can run more than once. Compute state purely, then perform the side effect outside the setter.

diagnostics.title: Missing effect dependencies
diagnostics.message: `useCallback` can run with a stale `syncRaffle` & show your users old data.

diagnostics.title: Ref mutated during render
diagnostics.message: This ref is mutated during render. React can replay or discard render work, so the mutation can leak from UI that never commits.
diagnostics.help: Move ref writes into an event handler or effect. Render must stay pure because React can replay or discard it. The predictable null-guarded lazy initialization pattern remains supported.

diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.help: Put a version in the storage key (e.g. "myKey:v1"). If you change the data shape later, old saved data can be ignored instead of crashing the app.

diagnostics.title: Loading flag reset outside finally
diagnostics.message: This resets a loading/busy flag only on the success path: if the awaited call rejects the reset never runs and the flag stays stuck truthy (a spinner that never stops, a button disabled forever). Move the reset into a `finally` block, or mirror it on every catch, so it clears on rejection too.
diagnostics.help: A trailing `setLoading(false)` after an `await` never runs if the awaited call rejects, so the flag stays stuck truthy; reset it in a `finally` block (or mirror the reset on every catch) so it clears on both paths.

diagnostics.title: Async mutating handler without re-entry guard
diagnostics.message: This async handler awaits a mutating request and only flips state after the await, so a fast double-click or double Enter fires the request twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard (or set a flag before the await and disable the control) to close the re-entry window.
diagnostics.help: An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.

diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: Data fetching inside an effect
diagnostics.message: fetch() inside useEffect can race, double-fire, or leak. Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component instead.
diagnostics.help: Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.title: Missing effect dependencies
diagnostics.message: `useEffect` can run with a stale `isPlaying` & show your users old data.

diagnostics.title: Boolean toggle reads a stale value
diagnostics.message: You can lose this update because setIsPlaying(!isPlaying) reads a stale value; use setIsPlaying(previous => !previous).
diagnostics.help: Toggle boolean state with the functional updater `setX(previous => !previous)` so deferred callbacks always read the latest committed value.

diagnostics.title: Pure function rebuilt every render
diagnostics.message: `formatTime` inside `FeaturedTrack` uses no local state but is rebuilt on every render, so it wastes work & breaks memoized children. Move it to the top of the file, outside the component.
diagnostics.help: Move the function above the component, at the top of the file. It doesn't use local state, so rebuilding it each update is wasted work.

diagnostics.title: Loading flag reset outside finally
diagnostics.message: This resets a loading/busy flag only on the success path: if the awaited call rejects the reset never runs and the flag stays stuck truthy (a spinner that never stops, a button disabled forever). Move the reset into a `finally` block, or mirror it on every catch, so it clears on rejection too.
diagnostics.help: A trailing `setLoading(false)` after an `await` never runs if the awaited call rejects, so the flag stays stuck truthy; reset it in a `finally` block (or mirror the reset on every catch) so it clears on both paths.

diagnostics.title: Effect promise .then sets state with no catch
diagnostics.message: This promise chain runs in an effect, ends in a `.then` that sets state or mutates a ref, and has no `.catch` or enclosing try/catch, so a rejection leaves the state unset and surfaces as an unhandled rejection. Add a `.catch` handler on the chain (`.finally` does not count).
diagnostics.help: An async init in an effect that sets state in `.then` but has no `.catch` leaves the component stuck and raises an unhandled rejection when it fails. Add a `.catch` on the chain (`.finally` does not handle the rejection).

diagnostics.title: Effect subscription or timer never cleaned up
diagnostics.message: `on` creates a subscription in useEffect without guaranteed cleanup. Return a cleanup function that owns every allocation so it does not leak after unmount.
diagnostics.help: Return a cleanup function that stops the subscription or timer: `return () => target.removeEventListener(name, handler)` for listeners, `return () => clearInterval(id)` or `clearTimeout(id)` for timers, `return () => observer.disconnect()` for observers, `return () => socket.close()` for connections, or `return unsubscribe` if the subscribe call already gave you one.

diagnostics.title: Ref mutated during render
diagnostics.message: This ref is mutated during render. React can replay or discard render work, so the mutation can leak from UI that never commits.
diagnostics.help: Move ref writes into an event handler or effect. Render must stay pure because React can replay or discard it. The predictable null-guarded lazy initialization pattern remains supported.
